reasoning: The package follows standard AUR packaging practices. The .install script uses setcap to grant necessary network capabilities to gst-ptp-helper, which is expected and legitimate behavior for GStreamer. The disagreement was solely caused by a transient API error in one of the models.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen model encountered an HTTP 400 API error when attempting to audit lib32-gstreamer.install, forcing an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully processed the same file and correctly identified the setcap commands as standard, non-malicious packaging behavior.
coverage_issues: Both models incorrectly skipped 0001-HACK-meson-Disable-broken-tests.patch by misidentifying it as a binary file. Patch files are plain text and must be audited to prevent build-time code injection.
The qwen model failed to audit lib32-gstreamer.install due to an unhandled API error.
false_negatives: The patch file was skipped by both models. While it is likely a benign test-disabling patch, skipping patches creates a blind spot for potential build-time injection.
learnings: The file type detection logic incorrectly classifies .patch files as binary. The tool should explicitly whitelist .patch and .diff extensions as text files to ensure they are passed to the LLM for auditing.
Implement retry logic or graceful degradation for transient LLM API errors (e.g., HTTP 400) so that a single file failure does not invalidate the entire package audit.
